summary.en: What money really is, where it comes from, where it goes, and why it slowly loses value.
summary.bs: Šta je zapravo novac, odakle dolazi, gdje odlazi i zašto polako gubi vrijednost.

en.one: Money is something everyone agrees to accept in exchange for things.
en.explain: Before money, people traded goods directly, like a chicken for a pair of shoes. That was hard. Money fixes this: you sell your work for money, then use the money to buy what you need. Money also lets you compare prices and save value for later.
en.example: A baker does not need to find a shoemaker who wants bread. She sells bread for €2 and uses those €2 to buy anything.
en.why: Every business idea comes down to money moving in and out. Understanding what money does helps you understand everything else.
en.mixup: Money is not the same as wealth. Wealth is everything you own, like a house or a business. Money is only one part of it.

bs.one: Novac je nešto što svi prihvataju u zamjenu za stvari.
bs.explain: Prije novca ljudi su mijenjali robu direktno, npr. kokoš za par cipela. To je bilo teško. Novac to rješava: prodaš svoj rad za novac, pa tim novcem kupiš šta ti treba. Novac ti također pomaže da porediš cijene i sačuvaš vrijednost za kasnije.
bs.example: Pekarka ne mora tražiti obućara kojem treba hljeb. Proda hljeb za 2 € i tih 2 € potroši na šta god želi.
bs.why: Svaka poslovna ideja se svodi na novac koji ulazi i izlazi. Kad razumiješ šta novac radi, lakše razumiješ sve ostalo.
bs.mixup: Novac nije isto što i bogatstvo. Bogatstvo je sve što posjeduješ, npr. kuća ili firma. Novac je samo jedan dio toga.

en.one: Income is money coming in. Expenses are money going out.
en.explain: For a person, income is your salary. Expenses are rent, food and bills. For a business, income comes from selling things, and expenses are everything it pays for to keep running. The goal is simple: more in than out.
en.example: You earn €1,500 a month. Rent, food and transport cost €1,200. You have €300 left.
en.why: This is the most basic health check for a person or a business. If expenses are bigger than income for long, you run into trouble.
en.mixup: Income is not the same as profit. Profit is what is left after expenses.

bs.one: Prihod je novac koji ulazi. Rashod je novac koji izlazi.
bs.explain: Za osobu, prihod je plata. Rashodi su kirija, hrana i računi. Za firmu, prihod dolazi od prodaje, a rashodi su sve što firma plaća da bi radila. Cilj je jednostavan: više da uđe nego da izađe.
bs.example: Zarađuješ 1.500 € mjesečno. Kirija, hrana i prevoz koštaju 1.200 €. Ostane ti 300 €.
bs.why: Ovo je najosnovnija provjera zdravlja za osobu ili firmu. Ako su rashodi duže vrijeme veći od prihoda, nastaju problemi.
bs.mixup: Prihod nije isto što i dobit. Dobit je ono što ostane nakon rashoda.

concepts.youtubeQuery: why saving money matters explained simply

en.one: Saving means keeping part of your money instead of spending it now.
en.explain: When you save, you give up a little today so you have more options tomorrow. Savings protect you when something unexpected happens and give you money to invest or grow a business.
en.example: You put aside €100 every month. After one year you have €1,200 ready for an emergency or an opportunity.
en.why: Businesses save too. They keep a cash cushion so a slow month does not become a crisis.
en.mixup: Saving is not the same as investing. Saving keeps money safe. Investing puts money to work, with some risk.

bs.one: Štednja znači da dio novca zadržiš umjesto da ga odmah potrošiš.
bs.explain: Kad štediš, odrekneš se malo danas da bi sutra imao više izbora. Ušteđevina te štiti kad se desi nešto neočekivano i daje ti novac za ulaganje ili rast biznisa.
bs.example: Svaki mjesec odvojiš 100 €. Nakon godinu dana imaš 1.200 € spremnih za hitan slučaj ili priliku.
bs.why: I firme štede. Drže rezervu novca da slab mjesec ne postane kriza.
bs.mixup: Štednja nije isto što i ulaganje. Štednja čuva novac. Ulaganje stavlja novac da radi, uz određeni rizik.

en.one: Inflation means prices go up over time, so the same money buys less.
en.explain: If inflation is 5% a year, something that costs €100 today will cost about €105 next year. Your €100 note did not change, but it buys a little less.
en.example: A coffee cost €1.50 a few years ago. Now it costs €2. That is inflation in your daily life.
en.why: Inflation quietly eats savings kept as cash. Businesses also need to raise prices over time, or their profit shrinks.
en.mixup: One product getting more expensive is not inflation. Inflation is when prices in general go up.

bs.one: Inflacija znači da cijene vremenom rastu, pa isti novac kupi manje.
bs.explain: Ako je inflacija 5% godišnje, nešto što danas košta 100 € iduće godine će koštati oko 105 €. Tvojih 100 € se nije promijenilo, ali kupi malo manje.
bs.example: Kafa je prije nekoliko godina koštala 1,50 €. Sad košta 2 €. To je inflacija u tvom svakodnevnom životu.
bs.why: Inflacija tiho jede ušteđevinu koju držiš u gotovini. Firme također moraju vremenom dizati cijene, inače im se dobit smanjuje.
bs.mixup: Kad samo jedan proizvod poskupi, to nije inflacija. Inflacija je kad cijene općenito rastu.
